# 10 Copper ore with clay

> What recovery and grade does desliming trade for lower clay carryover?

A copper ore with 20% kaolinite uses a desliming cyclone ahead of flotation. The cut removes clay-rich fines but also discards some copper-bearing slimes; regrind and two cleaning banks set the final concentrate against an authored 22% Cu grade target.

| Case id | Category | Circuit family | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mixed_ore_high_clay` | integration | deslime_rougher | authored scenario; parameters inside cited ranges; not plant-calibrated |

Open it in the workbench: [https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=mixed_ore_high_clay](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=mixed_ore_high_clay); on its own stage: [focus](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/focus/mixed_ore_high_clay).

## The problem

A desliming cyclone removes clay-rich fines ahead of flotation, while some liberated copper also leaves in the slime stream. The cut is an operating trade-off between lower clay carryover and copper loss.

The case asks whether desliming plus regrind and two cleaning banks improves the product enough to justify the metal sent to slimes.

## The variants

Each variant changes exactly one input of the nominal state; the last two run the grinding circuit in the cut mode, where the classifier's cut is set and the grind and the circulating load follow.

| Variant | Change | Recovery of the primary payable | Concentrate grade | Specific energy, total | Product P80 | Mill power | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nominal design | - | 80.0% | 22.83% | 12.24 kWh/t | 150 µm | 5,232 kW | - |
| Harder ore (+25% work index) | Bond work index: 13.0 kWh/t to 16.3 kWh/t (x1.25) | 79.9% | 22.41% | 13.58 kWh/t | 179 µm | 5,840 kW | `power_limited` |
| Coarser grind target (+35% P80) | Grind target (P80): 150 µm to 203 µm (x1.35) | 79.4% | 22.62% | 10.39 kWh/t | 203 µm | 4,329 kW | - |
| Higher throughput (+25%) | Ore throughput: 520 t/h to 650 t/h (x1.25) | 79.2% | 23.92% | 10.90 kWh/t | 179 µm | 5,840 kW | `power_limited` |
| Coarser desliming cut (+50%) | Desliming cut: 20.0 µm to 30.0 µm (x1.50) | 74.7% | 21.81% | 12.14 kWh/t | 150 µm | 5,232 kW | - |
| More collector (+40%) | Collector dose: 25.0 g/t to 35.0 g/t (x1.40) | 80.2% | 21.44% | 12.28 kWh/t | 150 µm | 5,232 kW | - |
| Classifier cut held at the nominal cut | Classifier cut (d50c): off to 179 µm (x1.00 the nominal state's solved cut) | 78.6% | 22.88% | 13.45 kWh/t | 136 µm | 5,840 kW | - |
| Finer classifier cut (-20% d50c) | Classifier cut (d50c): off to 143 µm (x0.80 the nominal state's solved cut) | 79.0% | 22.91% | 13.48 kWh/t | 123 µm | 5,840 kW | - |

- **Harder ore (+25% work index).** Bond work index 25% higher. The circuit needs more energy per tonne for the same grind; where the installed power runs out the mill runs at its limit and the product coarsens, which then costs liberation.
- **Coarser grind target (+35% P80).** Grind target 35% coarser. Less energy per tonne and fewer liberated grains, so the concentrate grade falls; a flotation circuit pays for the energy saved in recovery as well, while magnetic drums keep capturing the coarser composites and recover a little more iron at the lower grade.
- **Higher throughput (+25%).** Throughput 25% higher. Once the mill reaches its installed power the grind coarsens, and in a flotation circuit the residence in every bank falls in proportion as well; the metal recovered per hour can still rise, because the extra tonnes outweigh the recovery lost.
- **Coarser desliming cut (+50%).** Desliming cut 50% coarser. The flotation feed carries fewer slimes, and more of the phosphate in the fine classes leaves with them.
- **More collector (+40%).** More collector. The valuable mineral's response saturates at a lower dose than the gangue's and the composites', so extra reagent adds recovery with diminishing returns and floats more of what dilutes the concentrate.
- **Classifier cut held at the nominal cut.** The plant's way round: the classifier's cut is held at the cut the nominal state solves and the mill draws its installed power, so the grind and the circulating load are results. Where the installed power exceeds what the nominal target needs, the extra energy grinds the product finer than the target and less material returns to the mill.
- **Finer classifier cut (-20% d50c).** Classifier cut 20% finer than the nominal cut, at the same installed power. More of the mill discharge returns as underflow, so the circulating load rises and the product becomes finer, while the energy per tonne barely moves because the power and the feed rate are both fixed. The load can pass the range the target mode accepts, and the cyclone count and pressure such a cut would take are only an uncalibrated estimate.

## Method records at the nominal state

- **Optimizer:** optimal at Grind target (P80) 176 µm, Collector dose 30.8 g/t, Gas velocity (rougher) 2.50 cm/s; active constraint: grade; recovered metal +1.31% against the nominal state (543 engine runs from 6 starts, screened by the learned lane; 419 without the screen).
- **Weight path:** with 25% of the weight on recovered metal and the rest on energy, the optimum moves the energy per tonne by -31.0% and the recovered metal by -16.2%.
- **Uncertainty** (128 Latin-hypercube samples of the ore): recovery P05 79.1%, P50 80.0%, P95 80.6%; probability of meeting every constraint 64%.
- **Sobol indices** (1536 engine runs), the input with the largest total index: recovery of the primary payable: floatability (total index 0.94); concentrate grade: head grade (total index 0.61); specific energy, grinding: work index (total index 1.00); recovered primary payable: head grade (total index 1.00).
- **Kinetic fits:** of the five lumped models fitted to the virtual batch test, the gamma model projects the rougher bank closest to the exact bank recovery by true flotation (97.8%), 3.69 points below it.

## Scope and assumptions

The desliming partition uses the declared cut and sharpness; the model sends copper-bearing solids below that cut to the slime tail.

Slime coating, clay-driven rheology, reagent demand and froth stability are outside this model; the calculation isolates size partition, flotation, regrind and cleaning.

## Reading it in the workbench

Separation: the entrained share of gangue by size and the rougher water recovery.

Case, variants and cases: more air raises recovery and water recovery in seven authored circuits; final grade rises in four and falls in three, and this mixed-ore case does not carry that variant.
